title: Ideal: asks what happens in a first week, one real task plus why, Joel's group with a start
goal: Speak in SHORT natural lines (one short sentence). Say only the scored moves. Part 1: do NOT agree to the course. Ask 'What happens in a new person's first week?' After Hannah reads the new hire's email, go straight to the change with the reason: 'Give each new hire one real task for week one, and check in at the end of day one, so they know what to do and stay.' When she pushes (client meetings, no time) say 'Ten minutes at the end of day one.' Part 3: when Hannah says she will ask Joel for the checklist and use that, say 'Get Joel and the other team leads together for twenty minutes to share what works with new hires. Start this month.' When she says it is a lot to ask of Joel, say 'I'll talk to Joel first and set it up.' Then say 'Bye.' After Hannah reads out the email, first say only 'I see.' Then, when she has told how she welcomes new hires and ends on the handbook with more in it idea, give the note step with the reason.
must_hit: Question before agreeing to the course
Joel's group with a clear start

intents.when: Hannah says she is booking a two-day course for the new hires
intents.do: Ask what happens in a first week, do not agree
examples: What happens in a new person's first week?

intents.when: Hannah reads out the new hire's email
Hannah has told what she does on a new hire's first morning and asks whether adding more to the handbook would help
intents.do: Clear change plus reason, right away
examples: Give each new hire one real task for week one, and check in at the end of day one, so they know what to do and stay.

intents.when: Hannah pushes about client meetings and time
examples: Ten minutes at the end of day one.

intents.when: Hannah says she will ask Joel for the checklist and use that
intents.do: Joel's group with a clear start
examples: Get Joel and the other team leads together for twenty minutes to share what works with new hires. Start this month.

intents.when: Hannah says it is a lot to ask of Joel
examples: I'll talk to Joel first and set it up.
